claim_or_detail: PRC annual facilitation quota: each person may settle FX and each DOMESTIC individual may buy FX up to USD 50,000 equivalent per year with ID only; above-quota transactions need transaction documents.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 54–55 (also Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 2)

topic_or_title: PRC classification of a US citizen
claim_or_detail: A foreign national who has been continuously resident in the PRC for one year or more counts as a domestic individual (境内个人) under PRC FX rules; below one year the person is an overseas individual (境外个人).
locator: State Council Order No. 532, Art. 52(2)

claim_or_detail: Overseas individuals convert lawful RMB current-account income earned in China (e.g., employment pay) into FX at a bank with valid ID plus transaction-bearing source-of-funds materials that include a tax voucher (税务凭证); the bank then handles the outward current-account remittance under its document rules.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 59 ¶1 (quoted verbatim by SAFE Tianjin S01; remittance side: Art. 65)

claim_or_detail: Overseas individuals who hold a Foreigner's Permanent Residence ID (外国人永久居留身份证) use the annual facilitation quota for FX purchases.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 59 ¶2 (in gazette S06) + SAFE Tianjin 2024-06-21 Q&A

claim_or_detail: Domestic individuals: FX-account remittance for current account up to USD 50,000 equivalent same day needs ID only (above: transaction documents); FX cash remittance up to USD 10,000 same day needs ID (above: customs-stamped declaration or original withdrawal slip plus documents). Overseas individuals: FX-account remittance needs valid ID; FX cash remittance up to USD 10,000 same day needs ID (above: customs-stamped declaration or original withdrawal slip).
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 64–65 (same structure in Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 14–15)

claim_or_detail: An overseas individual may reconvert previously exchanged but UNUSED RMB back to FX with ID plus the original exchange slip (兑换水单) within 24 months of exchange; without the slip, only same-day conversions up to USD 500 equivalent (USD 1,000 at domestic-offshore locations before departure) are ID-only.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 60 (quoted verbatim by SAFE Tianjin 2026-09-17; also in gazette S06)

claim_or_detail: Individuals must not split transactions (分拆) to evade the facilitation-quota or truthfulness requirements. Lending your quota triggers a risk warning, then watch-list (关注名单) status on repetition; borrowing others' quota puts you on the watch list directly; listing lasts the year of listing plus the following 2 years, during which all FX settlement/purchase requires transaction documents.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 62–63 (also Art. 47 for service trade)

topic_or_title: PRC bank refusal — get it in writing
claim_or_detail: Banks must reasonably review transaction documents for personal current-account FX, may refuse transactions that violate FX rules or whose authenticity is doubtful, and must state the refusal reason accurately and provide the appeal channel.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 68

topic_or_title: PRC tax-filing gate on large service payments
claim_or_detail: Outward service-trade payments above USD 50,000 equivalent by domestic institutions AND individuals require prior tax-filing (税务备案) procedures, and the bank verifies the tax filing form.

FX cash withdrawal from a bank up to USD 10,000 equivalent same day: ID only; above that: ID plus withdrawal-purpose evidence with prior SAFE filing (提取外币现钞备案表). FX cash deposits and cash-convert settlements: up to USD 10,000 same day handled per identity/document rules; above requires customs-stamped declaration or the original withdrawal slip.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 86–88; supersession clause in the issuing notice; Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 30–31 for the earlier USD 5,000 deposit figure

claim_or_detail: Carrying foreign currency INTO China above USD 5,000 equivalent requires a written customs declaration (and any second-or-later crossing in a short period requires it regardless of amount). Carrying FX OUT: amounts between USD 5,000 and 10,000 beyond the recorded inbound amount require a bank-issued Carry Permit for Foreign Exchange (携带外汇出境许可证); above USD 10,000 (for qualifying destinations) requires a SAFE-issued permit.
locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 89 (bank/SAFE permit system also in Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 5)

claim_or_detail: PRC FX penalties (statutory maxima): evading FX controls (逃汇) — fine up to 30% of the amount, or 30% up to the equivalent amount if serious, criminal liability possible; illegal FX arbitrage via false documents (非法套汇) — same 30% structure; private/improper buying-selling or brokering FX in large amounts — warning, confiscation of gains, fine up to 30%, 30%+ if serious, criminal liability; operating settlement/sale FX business without approval — confiscation of gains plus 1–5× gains if gains ≥ CNY 500,000, or CNY 500,000–2,000,000 if no/low gains, license suspension/revocation, criminal liability; carrying FX across the border in violation — warning plus fine up to 20% of the amount.
locator: State Council Order No. 532, Art. 39, 40, 45, 46, 42

claim_or_detail: PRC policy imposes no restriction in principle on current-account international payments and transfers; current-account FX income may be retained or sold, and current-account payments are made with valid documents.
locator: State Council Order No. 532, Art. 5, 12–14

claim_or_detail: PRC individual income tax: a person domiciled in China or present ≥183 days in a tax year is a resident and taxed on worldwide income; comprehensive income (wages etc.) is taxed at 3%–45% progressive rates with a CNY 60,000 annual standard deduction (non-residents: CNY 5,000/month); interest, dividends, property rental/transfer and incidental income are taxed at a flat 20%.
locator: PRC IIT Law, Art. 1, 3, 6 (2018 amendment)

claim_or_detail: PRC residents may credit foreign income tax paid against PRC tax on foreign-source income, capped at the PRC tax computed on that income under the IIT Law.
locator: PRC IIT Law, Art. 7

topic_or_title: Conversion-penalty layer — is there a PRC tax on converting?
claim_or_detail: In the PRC instruments reviewed for this check (State Council Order No. 532; Hui Fa [2007] No. 1; Hui Fa [2020] No. 14) no standalone tax on the act of currency conversion was located — those instruments impose identity, document, quota and penalty rules instead. Any PRC tax due follows the underlying income (V14), not the conversion itself.
locator: Absence check across S04, S05, S06 (full texts re-read this session)

claim_or_detail: US citizens and resident aliens living abroad are taxed on worldwide income; a foreign earned income exclusion may apply if the bona fide residence test or the 330-day physical presence test is met, with amounts adjusted annually for inflation (fetched page lists $107,600 for 2020 through $120,000 for 2023).
locator: IRS 'Foreign earned income exclusion' (page 1)

topic_or_title: US currency-gain rule on personal conversions
claim_or_detail: Under 26 U.S.C. §988, gains or losses on foreign-currency transactions are ordinary income/loss, and disposing of nonfunctional currency (including bank deposits) is a §988 transaction — BUT for individuals, personal transactions are outside §988, and in a personal disposal no gain is recognized due to exchange-rate movement unless the gain would exceed $200.

A US person with a financial interest in, or signature/other authority over, foreign financial accounts must file the FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) if the aggregate value exceeded USD 10,000 at any time during the calendar year; due April 15 with automatic extension to October 15; account income is irrelevant; civil and/or criminal penalties apply, with civil maxima adjusted annually for inflation.
locator: IRS FBAR page + 31 CFR 1010.350 (S12)

claim_or_detail: Form 8938 thresholds for specified foreign financial assets: living in the US — unmarried/married-filing-separate more than $50,000 at year end or $75,000 at any time; married filing jointly more than $100,000/$150,000. Living abroad — unmarried more than $200,000/$300,000; married filing jointly more than $400,000/$600,000. Filing Form 8938 does not relieve FBAR duties.
locator: IRS FATCA summary, 'Reporting thresholds' section

topic_or_title: US foreign tax credit vs exclusion
claim_or_detail: US citizens may claim a foreign tax credit (Form 1116) for qualifying foreign income taxes instead of an itemized deduction; no credit is allowed for tax on income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion; where a treaty reduces the foreign tax rate, only the reduced amount qualifies for the credit.
locator: IRS 'Foreign Tax Credit' page sections 'Qualifying foreign taxes', 'Compliance issues'

claim_or_detail: The US–China income tax treaty (in force since 1 January 1987) caps source-state tax on dividends, interest and royalties at 10% of the gross amount in each case (for beneficial owners), and the residence state gives credit for the other state's tax; a saving clause sits in Protocol 1.
locator: Treaty Arts. 9, 10, 11, 22; Letter of Submittal; Protocol 1 saving clause

claim_or_detail: There is no legal limit on how much currency or monetary instruments a traveler may carry into or out of the United States, but amounts of $10,000 or greater (combined) must be reported to CBP on FinCEN Form 105 (electronic filing at fincen105.cbp.dhs.gov); non-reporting risks seizure plus civil and/or criminal penalties (31 USC 5316).
locator: CBP official releases (S14 2025; corroborating S15 2017)
